context:
Goal: a ready PR does not sit waiting behind other work to merge.
Problem (rule): session-tiers.md line 114, Batch runner bullet, says the runner "marks ready only while no job is queued". Your 18:10 CST Nov 15 words (relayed by the consultant, not read as typed): "in general things shouldnt have had to wait for other stuff behind to merge imagine sand shifting through multiple strainers in a sense man cmon we’ve talked abt this". Whether that overturns the gate fully or only for unrelated PRs is not settled; runner 10 keeps its gate meanwhile (coordinator told it).
Based on (measured): runner 10 14:12 CST Nov 15: the gate cost 53 to 81 min from mark to merge, n=3, limit was the CI queue (relayed).
Based on (ruling): own-ready-pr-no-queue-wait (relayed, filed 345d86753).
Departs from: main — the runner marks ready only while no job is queued; this changes when it may mark.
A related fact: #3341's red ready run came from a stale merge ref (parents 685fa1631 + ec3aa9a22 before the revert), not from the gate (coordinator measured, n=1).

lastAnswer.note: Saved on the waiting page: B, overturn the ready gate only for pull requests that touch different areas.

options.how: The runner drops the no-queued-job condition; each PR goes ready once its head is current.
options.label: Overturn the gate fully: a PR goes ready as soon as its head is current
options.lose: Several full CI runs share the queue, so each takes longer and a red run is harder to blame.

options.gain: Unrelated PRs stop waiting; related ones still go one at a time.
options.how: PRs that touch different areas go ready together; related ones still go one at a time.
options.label: Overturn it only for PRs that touch different areas
options.lose: Runner 10 must first measure what counts as an area, so it starts later than option a.

options.gain: One run at a time, clear blame.
options.how: The runner keeps marking ready only while no job is queued.
options.label: Keep the gate as it is
options.lose: Your 18:10 CST words are not acted on; waits of 53 to 81 min stay.

ref: session-tiers Batch runner bullet (line 114), own-ready-pr-no-queue-wait, PR #3341
reply: Closed: you picked b on 18:37 CST Nov 15. The ruling own-ready-gate-unrelated-prs holds it, and runner 10 and the step ready-no-queue-wait carry the rest. A new, narrower question about queued macOS jobs is a separate item.
short: Ready gate: how far to overturn

shown.label: Overturn the gate fully: a PR goes ready as soon as its head is current
Overturn it only for PRs that touch different areas
Keep the gate as it is

title: Does "things shouldn't have to wait behind other PRs" overturn the batch runner's ready gate fully, or only for unrelated PRs?
why: The coordinator's lean (relayed): marks proceed one run at a time per area, measured by runner 10 first.
